statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is true if and only if len(nums) >= 2 and, with n = len(nums) - 1, for every integer x, the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = x is: 2 if x = n; 1 if 1 <= x < n; and 0 otherwise. Equivalently, r is true exactly when nums is a permutation of base[n] = [1, 2, ..., n-1, n, n] for n = len(nums) - 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 200.

statement: For any two slices nums and nums' satisfying the constraints, if for every integer x the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = x equals the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums') and nums'[i] = x, then whenever is_good(nums) returns r and is_good(nums') returns r', we have r = r'.
